subject: math
title: Statistics and Probability
syllabus: Measures of dispersion: calculation of mean, median, mode of grouped and ungrouped data, calculation of standard deviation, variance, and mean deviation for grouped and ungrouped data. Probability: probability of an event, addition and multiplication theorems of probability, Bayes theorem, probability distribution of a random variate.

body: Mean x̄ = \f{Σx}{n}. Median: middle value of sorted data (average of the two middles if n is even).
Variance σ^{2} = \f{Σx^{2}}{n} − x̄^{2}; SD = σ. Mean deviation = \f{Σ|x − c|}{n} about c = mean or median.
Unknown data values: use Σx = n·x̄ and Σx^{2} = n(σ^{2} + x̄^{2}) to get a + b and a^{2} + b^{2}.
y = ax + b: mean becomes a x̄ + b, variance a^{2}σ^{2}, SD |a|σ.
Wrong value w replaced by r: Σx changes by r − w, Σx^{2} by r^{2} − w^{2}; recompute.
Combining groups: add their Σx and Σx^{2}. A.P. with difference d and n terms has variance \f{d^{2}(n^{2} − 1)}{12}.
P(E) = \f{favourable}{total} for equally likely outcomes; list or count carefully (ordered vs unordered).
Complement: P(at least one) = 1 − P(none). Independent events multiply.
Selections: C(n, r); arrangements: P(n, r). Dice: 6^{n} outcomes.
E(X) = Σx p(x); Var(X) = Σx^{2}p(x) − (E X)^{2}. Probabilities add to 1 — use that to find k.
Binomial B(n, p): P(X = r) = C(n, r)p^{r}q^{n−r}, mean np, variance npq.
P(A | B) = \f{P(A ∩ B)}{P(B)}. Total probability: P(B) = Σ P(A_{i})P(B | A_{i}).
Bayes: P(A_{i} | B) = \f{P(A_{i})P(B | A_{i})}{Σ P(A_{j})P(B | A_{j})}.
Rare conditions: even an accurate test gives many false alarms when the base rate is small.

traps: Variance uses the mean of squares minus the square of the mean — not the reverse.
Adding a constant does not change variance or SD.
Mean deviation about the median needs the median, not the mean.
Without replacement the draws are not independent.
Ordered and unordered counts must match top and bottom.

A card from a pack of 52 cards is lost. From the remaining 51 cards, n cards are drawn and are found to be spades. If the probability of the lost card to be a spade is \f{11}{50}, then n is equal to ______.
sol: Bayes: P(lost spade | n spades drawn) = \f{\f{1}{4}C(12, n)}{\f{1}{4}C(12, n) + \f{3}{4}C(13, n)} = \f{13 − n}{52 − n}.

sol: P(black | A, B, C) = \f{5}{12}, \f{7}{12}, \f{6}{12}; urns equally likely.

sol: Two distinct real roots ⇔ b^{2} > 4ac; 216 equally likely triples.

sol: Repeated roots ⇔ b^{2} = 4ac, so b is even and ac = (\f{b}{2})^{2}.

From a lot of 12 items containing 3 defectives, a sample of 5 items is drawn at random. Let the random variable X denote the number of defective items in the sample. Let items in the sample be drawn one by one without replacement. If variance of X is \f{m}{n}, where gcd(m, n) = 1, then n − m is equal to ______.
sol: Hypergeometric with N = 12, D = 3, n = 5: Var = n·\f{D}{N}·\f{N − D}{N}·\f{N − n}{N − 1}.

sol: All bags have 9 coins and are equally likely.

pyq.q: Let a, b, c ∈ ℕ and a < b < c. Let the mean, the mean deviation about the mean and the variance of the 5 observations 9, 25, a, b, c be 18, 4 and \f{136}{5}, respectively. Then 2a + b − c is equal to ______.
sol: Mean 18 → a + b + c = 56. Variance: Σ(x − 18)^{2} = 136 → 81 + 49 + Σ(a, b, c deviations)^{2} = 136 → their squares add to 6.
Mean deviation: 9 + 7 + Σ|dev| = 20 → Σ|dev| = 4 with squares summing to 6 and deviations summing to 2 (to balance −9 + 7): −1, 1, 2.

Three balls are drawn at random from a bag containing 5 blue and 4 yellow balls. Let the random variables X and Y respectively denote the number of blue and Yellow balls. If X̄ and Ȳ are the means of X and Y respectively, then 7X̄ + 4Ȳ is equal to ______.
sol: Each ball is in the sample with chance \f{3}{9}: X̄ = \f{5}{3}, Ȳ = \f{4}{3}.

pyq.q: If the variance of the frequency distribution x: c, 2c, 3c, 4c, 5c, 6c with f: 2, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1 is 160, then the value of c ∈ ℕ is
sol: For c = 1 the data are 1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6: mean \f{22}{7}, mean of squares \f{92}{7} → variance \f{92}{7} − \f{484}{49} = \f{160}{49}.
Scaling by c multiplies the variance by c^{2}: \f{160}{49}c^{2} = 160 → c = 7.

pyq.q: If an unbiased dice is rolled thrice, then the probability of getting a greater number in the i^{th} roll than the number obtained in the (i − 1)^{th} roll, i = 2, 3, is equal to :
sol: Strictly increasing triples are just choices of 3 different faces: C(6, 3) = 20.

pyq.q: The frequency distribution of the age of students in a class of 40 students is: age 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20 with numbers 5, 8, 5, 12, x, y. If the mean deviation about the median is 1.25, then 4x + 5y is equal to :
sol: x + y = 10. Cumulative 5, 13, 18, 30: the 20th and 21st ages are 18 → median 18.

sol: Set {1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 5}. The smaller is ≥ 4 only if both come from {4, 5, 6}: 3·2 = 6 of 30 ordered pairs.

pyq.q: A man throws a fair coin repeatedly. He gets 10 points for each head he throws and 5 points for each tail he throws. If the probability that he gets exactly 30 points is \f{m}{n}, gcd(m, n) = 1, then m + n is equal to:
sol: In units of 5 points each toss adds 1 (tail) or 2 (head). Let p_{n} = P(the running total ever equals n).

pyq.q: The mean and variance of n observations are 8 and 16, respectively. If the sum of the first (n − 1) observations is 48 and the sum of squares of the first (n − 1) observations is 496, then the value of n is :
sol: Last observation x = 8n − 48; Σx^{2} = n(16 + 64) = 80n → x^{2} = 80n − 496.

sol: An A.P. with d = 13 and n = \f{320 − 8}{13} + 1 = 25 terms.

pyq.q: A coin is tossed 8 times. If the probability that exactly 4 heads appear in the first six tosses and exactly 3 heads appear in the last five tosses is p, then 96p is equal to ______.
sol: Tosses 4–6 are shared. Let k heads be among them: first three need 4 − k, last two need 3 − k.

sol: ab is not divisible by 3 only if neither is: 34 such numbers → C(34, 2) = 561 pairs.

From a month of 31 days, 3 different dates are selected at random. If the probability that these dates are in an increasing A.P. is equal to \f{a}{b}, where a, b ∈ ℕ and gcd(a, b) = 1, then a + b is equal to ______.
sol: Common difference d = 1, …, 15 gives 31 − 2d triples: total Σ(31 − 2d) = 465 − 240 = 225.

pyq.q: If the mean deviation about the median of the numbers k, 2k, 3k, …, 1000k is 500, then k^{2} is equal to :
sol: Median = 500.5k; for k = 1 the deviations of 1, …, 1000 from 500.5 add to 2(0.5 + 1.5 + … + 499.5) = 250000.

pyq.q: Let n be the number obtained on rolling a fair die. If the probability that the system x − ny + z = 6, x + (n − 2)y + (n + 1)z = 8, (n − 1)y + z = 1 has a unique solution is \f{k}{6}, then the sum of k and all possible values of n is :
sol: Unique solution ⇔ determinant ≠ 0. R_{2} − R_{1}: (0, 2n − 2, n); with row (0, n − 1, 1): det = (2n − 2) − n(n − 1) = −(n − 1)(n − 2).

pyq.q: A letter is known to have arrived by post either from KANPUR or from ANANTPUR. On the envelope just two consecutive letters AN are visible. The probability, that the letter came from ANANTPUR, is:
sol: KANPUR has 5 consecutive pairs, one AN: \f{1}{5}. ANANTPUR has 7 pairs, two AN: \f{2}{7}.

A variable X takes values 0, 0, 2, 6, 12, 20, …, n(n − 1) with frequencies ^{n}C_{0}, ^{n}C_{1}, ^{n}C_{2}, ^{n}C_{3}, ^{n}C_{4}, ^{n}C_{5}, …, ^{n}C_{n}, respectively. If the mean of this data is 60, then its median is :
sol: Value i(i − 1) has frequency C(n, i). ΣC(n, i)i(i − 1) = n(n − 1)2^{n−2}, total 2^{n} → mean \f{n(n − 1)}{4} = 60 → n = 16.
The middle of 2^{16} observations falls in the i = 8 block (the symmetric centre of C(16, i)).

pyq.q: The mean and variance of 10 observations are 9 and 34.2, respectively. If 8 of these observations are 2, 3, 5, 10, 11, 13, 15, 21, then the mean deviation about the median of all the 10 observations is
sol: Missing two: sum 90 − 80 = 10; Σx^{2} = 10(34.2 + 81) = 1152 → their squares add to 1152 − 1094 = 58 → 3 and 7.
